title: fix(objectql, metadata-protocol)!: by-name doors judge a name's holders over the served set, so a disabled package's item is not a holder (ADR-0150 D3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB4A4i75GS3izWa4tjti3Tav)_

Fixes #32183

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — for a name that only disabled packages hold, `SchemaRegistry.resolveItem`, `MetadataFacade.get` / `getEntry` and `SchemaRegistry.getApp` (`@objectstack/objectql`) answer `undefined` where they answered the disabled package's body, and `MetadataFacade.exists` answers false where it answered true. Every by-name door already withheld that body. The other moved answers are listed in the changeset, each before → after. Most widen or name fewer packages: a name one enabled and one disabled package hold is served by the enabled holder where it was refused naming both. One narrows a served answer to a refusal: a package caller whose closure holds the name only through a disabled package, while an enabled package outside the closure holds it, is refused `outside-closure` where it was served the disabled package's body. The rest move between a refusal and not-found.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx` already says a disabled module is hidden, and no skill or doc teaches the by-name answer for a name a disabled package holds.

**Narrowing: yes** — first-party callers: **0** (measured). `MetadataFacade` is never constructed in-tree, `SchemaRegistry.getApp` has no in-tree caller, and the one door that reads `resolveItem` (the protocol's by-name read) already withheld a disabled package's body. The served → refused move and the resolver primitives' moves need a disabled package, and no first-party app disables one at boot. On showcase (22 packages, 205 package-scoped names), crm (18, 35) and multi-package (16, 27), no name has two holders and no package is disabled at boot.

Claim by `domain:server#3`; seat GO with rulings (a)–(c) in claim amendment 6773105294; step-0 readings in 6773035227. Child of epic #31527 (ADR-0150 D3).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：按名读取包作用域元数据时，「持有者」现在只算正在提供服务的包。已停用包的条目不再算持有者：一个名字由一个启用包和一个停用包同时持有时，由启用包作答，不再 409 列出两者；只有停用包持有的名字等同无人持有（404 或未找到），不再点名停用包。存储引用回填、CLI 存储引用报告、选项列表（picklist）判定这类持久判断仍读全部持有者，所以停用是可逆的，绑定不会跟着停用移动。
- 为什么改：列表读取早已隐藏停用包的条目，按名读取却还把它算作持有者，于是同一个名字在列表里只有一个、按名读却被 409 拒绝，或者拒绝信息点名一个看不见的包（ADR-0150 D3，史诗 #31527）。
- 风险与回滚：多数答案是放宽（409 变 200）。收窄在进程内库 API：只有停用包持有的名字，`resolveItem`、`MetadataFacade.get` 和 `getApp` 返回 `undefined`，`exists` 返回 false；一个包调用方只经由停用包才够得着某个名字、而闭包外有启用包持有时，从「得到停用包的条目」变为 `outside-closure` 拒绝。第一方调用方 0：第一方示例里没有两个包同名、也没有启动即停用的包。回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`（`packageScopedHoldersOf` 的 served 过滤与 `picklistReferenceVerdict`），然后 `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`（只有停用包持有的名字仍按停用包的被扣留条目作答，分层视图和 `/published` 不会把它端出来），最后 `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts`（停用持有者的列不改指向）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/package-scoped-resolver.test.ts src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts`，预期全部通过，其中 `#32183` 开头的几节逐级钉住。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **The holder set is the served set** (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packageScopedHoldersOf`). A holder whose package is disabled (`isPackageDisabled`, the predicate `listItems` hides by) is left out, except the caller's own holding. `options.includeDisabledPackages: true` (the option name `listItems` already carries) reads every holder. A disable never promotes a dependent's bundle addition to a holder: the addition test still runs over every holder. `resolvePackageScopedName`'s query takes `includeDisabledPackages` and forwards it, and so do the action addressing wrapper and the install door's pending-manifest view.
- **Durable judgments read every holder**, so a stored binding never moves with a reversible disable:
  - the stored-reference backfills: permission sets (`plugin-security`), sharing declarations (`plugin-sharing`), email templates (`plugin-email`) and the activation ledger (`objectql`);
  - the CLI stored-reference report (`os migrate stored-references`, `packages/cli/src/utils/stored-package-references.ts`);
  - `picklistReferenceVerdict`, which the kernel:ready load audit, the install door and a field's options fold share. A disable never refuses the next boot and never empties a live field's options.
- **The security catalog** (`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts`):
  - a stored column naming a package that still holds the set but is disabled is not-found, never re-targeted to the enabled holder;
  - a name only disabled packages hold is not-found, never the metadata service's by-name body;
  - `holdsPlatformPermissionSet` answers false for that name.
- **The item face** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`, `readMetaItemFace`): when the read finds no item and every package holding the name is disabled, the face answers it as that package's withheld item: `item` undefined, the envelope's `packageId` naming the disabled holder. That is the shape a disabled holder's read had on `main`. Without it, the bare read of such a name carried no package, so the layered view's step 1b and `/published` (which ask the envelope whether a disable withheld the item, on both transports) took it as not withheld. `/layers` then served the disabled package's code layer at the bare address and at `?package=` of any non-holder, and `/published` served its snapshot. The rest suite caught it (`meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts`).
- **The bare reads take the served holder's stack** (fix round, contract review M1; `protocol-meta-item-face.ts` `servedHolderAddressOf`, `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`). A read naming no package, of a name an enabled and a disabled package both hold, is read at the enabled holder's address: the plain read, the layered read's code layer, overlay row and lock, and the layered row-ambiguity refusal (which no longer refuses a read the served holder addresses). Before, the layered code layer was the first composite in registration order, the disabled holder's when it registered first, and a legacy row bound to the disabled holder made the bare read answer 404.
- **R7–R11 read every holder** (fix round, M2). The approval-request, paused-run, flow-credential, dispatch-key and connector-connection backfills now ask `AutomationEngine.durableFlowHolder` (new) and the connector resolver with `includeDisabledPackages`. `FlowNameResolver` and `ConnectorNameResolver` take an optional `options` argument. `flowHolder` and the execute doors keep judging the served holders.
- **The metadata service's by-name copy** (fix round 2, contract review M4). The artifact door registers every package body's items in the metadata service. Its manager stores `agent`, `skill`, `api` and `action` per package and every other type by name alone, so for a name two packages ship it keeps the body registered last.
  - The redirected layered read drops a service copy stamped with another registry holder of the name (`isAnotherHoldersCopy`, `protocol-meta-item-face.ts`). The artifact lookup at the served holder's address is then the code layer.
  - Both `/published` doors (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) read the metadata service at the plain read's package for such a name. A copy stamped with another holder is replaced by the layered read's code layer at that address. A name with no copy in the service still answers 404, as for a single holder.
  - `MetadataManager.getPublished(type, name, packageId?)` (`@objectstack/metadata`) takes an optional package, read as `get` reads it.
  - Before, measured on a booted artifact kernel with the disabled body registered last: the dashboard's bare `/layers` code layer and `/published` were the disabled holder's, on both transports. The agent's `/published` was refused 409 naming the disabled package, in both orders.
- **The REST action rung** (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `resolveRouteActionByPackage`): a thrown package-scoped refusal (read through `refusalOf`, the reader #32213 added) becomes the declaration's `refusal`, answered as the declared `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Before, it was swallowed as `degraded`. No door reaches this rung: it runs only for a caller that names its package, and neither `domains/actions.ts` nor `action-dispatch.ts` passes one.
- **Nits** (fix round): `heldOnlyDisabled` in the security catalog is `heldInAnyPackage`; plugin-sharing's `listedHoldersView` and the runtime's `automation-address.ts` `holdersOf` forward the caller and `options`.
- **Changeset**: `patch` for objectql, metadata-protocol, core, runtime, cli, plugin-security, plugin-email, plugin-sharing, service-automation, plugin-approvals, rest and metadata, with the BREAKING banner, before → after lines for the library moves (the only-disabled readers, the resolver primitives, and the served → refused move) and one for every moved door answer, each with its first-party count, and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

### Owed before ACCEPT: the exact-qualifier hunk (ruling (c))

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` is not touched yet. It waits until #32277 and #32214 have both merged; then this branch merges `origin/main` (no rebase) and adds:

- admission over every holder (`includeDisabledPackages: true`), so `?package=DISABLED` reaches the item face and answers its 404;
- `resolveMetaItemAddress` falls back to a holding owner over every holder, so the disabled package's namespace path keeps its 404;
- pins: `?package=DISABLED`, `/meta/:type/DISABLED_NS/:name` and the `.custom` pair of a disabled base stay 404 on both transports and never name the enabled holder.

**Interim, at this head:** with two holders where one is disabled, `?package=DISABLED`, the disabled package's namespace path and the disabled base's `.custom` pair (`?package=DISABLED.custom`) answer 409 `not-held-by-qualifier` naming the enabled holder, where `main` answers 404. The pair's answer was measured on a booted artifact kernel, on both transports. The changeset's "Not moved" line describes the answer after the owed hunk.

## Why

The served list (`listItems`) has withheld a disabled package's items since the disable landed, and the item face answers 404 for one. But `packageScopedHoldersOf` read the raw store, so every ADR-0150 D3 door still counted the disabled package as a holder. A name the list showed once was refused 409 naming both packages at the bare read, and a name only a disabled package held was refused naming a package the caller cannot see. The epic ruling 6766102988 names the served list as the right holder set; plugin-sharing's `listedHoldersView` was the one door that already filtered.

## Tests

Each new block is a `#32183 — …` describe. All run over the real `SchemaRegistry` except the core catalog's, which uses the file's registry double.

- `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.test.ts`: `flow`, `app` and `page` with two holders, one disabled → the enabled one; a caller outside the closure; the caller's own disabled holding is kept; only-disabled → no holder; `includeDisabledPackages` reads both; re-enable restores the refusal; a disable never promotes a bundle addition.
- `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts`: the library readers over the live `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`, `getApp`, the MCP `agent_prompt` read, a caller outside the closure.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts` and `packages/rest/src/meta-qualified-item-route.test.ts`, for every type of the live `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`: two holders with one disabled → 200 with the enabled holder's item; only-disabled → 404 on the bare read, `_env`, `?package=NONHOLDER` and a non-holder's namespace path, never naming the disabled package; the parity pin (the by-name door and the list read agree on holders, through a disable and a re-enable); co-owners of a shareable namespace.
- The same two files, for every type: only disabled holders (one, and a name two disabled packages hold) → `/layers` answers 404 at the bare address, `?package=` of a non-holder and `?package=` of an enabled non-holder, serving no layer, and the plain read answers 404 naming neither; CONTROL: enabled, the layered view serves the code layer. The rest file's `beforeEach` wires the engine, so step 1b can ask the registry.
- `packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts`: the enabled holder's declaration; the rung answers the declared refusal.
- Fix round, M1: the two qualified-read files above, every type, both registration orders: the plain read and bare `/layers` serve the enabled holder's `code` and `effective`. `packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts` and the new `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts` (a booted kernel): the plain read, `/layers` and `/published`, both orders, with a legacy row bound to the disabled holder alone and with one bound to each holder.
- Fix round, M2: `packages/services/service-automation/src/stored-reference-package-column.test.ts` (R8–R11) and `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/stored-process-package-backfill.test.ts` (R7): a flow and a connector whose only holder is disabled bind to it; a clash with one holder disabled stays null naming both, in both orders; `flowHolder` and the connector resolver without the option keep the served answer.
- Fix round, S2 and M3: every two-holder family above now also registers the disabled holder first; `package-scoped-resolver.test.ts` pins the served → refused move.
- Fix round 2, M4: the new `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-artifact-door.test.ts`. A booted kernel loads a compiled artifact whose `packages[]` carries two bodies that ship one dashboard (stored by name) and one agent (stored per package). It runs both registration orders on both transports (`HttpDispatcher` and `RestServer` over the kernel's protocol). The fixture check confirms the service keeps the dashboard registered last. CONTROL: both enabled, every bare door is 409. One disabled: the plain read, `/layers` and `/published` serve the enabled holder's item. Re-enabled: 409 again. `meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts` adds `stamped_page`, whose snapshot copy is stamped with the disabled holder: its `/published` serves the enabled holder's code layer, and the snapshot is read at that package. `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-published-package.test.ts` pins `getPublished` with a package.
- Fix round, the action door: the new `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-disabled-holder-door.test.ts` (a booted kernel): two packages declare one action on one object, one disabled; the bare `POST /actions/:object/:action` runs the enabled holder's action in both orders and is refused 409 naming both once re-enabled.
- `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.test.ts`: a disabled holder's column is not-found and never re-targets; only-disabled is not-found and never reaches the metadata service; `holdsPlatformPermissionSet`.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-picklist.test.ts`: a disabled holder's picklist keeps the field's options, the load audit stays clear, and `resolveItem` answers `undefined`.
- The backfills (`activation-ledger-backfill`, `stored-template-package-backfill`, `stored-permission-set-package-backfill`, `stored-declaration-package-backfill`) and the CLI report (`stored-package-references.literal-namespace`, row R20 stays ambiguous naming both).

## Acceptance notes

- **A correction to my step-0 readings.** The readings labelled the install door's pending-manifest view (`registry.ts`, `withPendingManifests`) as "the picklist load audit". The load audit reads `picklistReferenceVerdict` on the plain registry. The build keeps that verdict over every holder (see What changes), and the view forwards the option.
- **A back door this branch opened, caught and fixed before the PR.** With the served holder set alone, the rest suite went red in `meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts` (2 tests): `/published` and `/layers` of a page only the disabled package ships answered 200. A probe showed the same at `?package=` of any non-holder on `/layers`. The step-0 census had not listed the doors that read the bare read's envelope. The item face fix above closes it; ablation A7 below.
- **Interim regression** until the owed hunk: see above.
- **Changeset wording.** The seat asked for FROM → TO lines. The labels read "Before → after", because the ADR-0087 gate reads an upper-case `FROM → TO` label as a migration prescription beside `no-migration-prescription`. Every moved answer still reads as before → after.
- **Not touched:** the install gate (`bareNamePackageHolders`, epic stance 6766291071) and the security catalog's item seam. Limbs 6767831853 and 6767803831 moved to #32292 (ruling (b)).
- **#32214's declared item 5** (the email template doors read the raw holder set) is closed by this change once both land, because the filter sits in `packageScopedHoldersOf`.
- **Dogfood battery:** owed once, on the final head after the qualifier hunk (narrowing arm).
- **Fix round (contract review 6776491373, rulings 6776508467).** M1, M2, M3, S1, S2, the action door and the nits as above; `main` merged at e31ea52a (conflicts in three test files, resolved keeping both sides).
- **Fix round 2 (contract review 6779367258).** M4, S3 and the interim paragraph as above. `main` merged again at 9bff554e, which carries #32277. Two test files conflicted, and both sides were kept. #32277's hunks in `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` and `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` are untouched.
- **Read-then-save of a mixed name** (the seat's probe, on a booted artifact kernel, both orders, through the protocol). The bare read answers the enabled holder. The bare save judges its address through `packagelessAddress`, which counts every stored row, and this diff does not change it.
  - No stored row: the read reports no version token, and the save writes a package-unbound row.
  - A row bound to the disabled holder alone: the read reports no overlay and no token, and the save is not refused. It updates the disabled holder's row.
  - A row bound to each holder: the read serves the enabled row with its token, and the save is refused 409 naming both and asking for `?package=`.

  Not fixed here. Where a save lands is a durable judgment, the same principle as R7–R11, so pointing the bare save at the served holder would move a write with a reversible disable. It needs its own ruling.
- **Carried, for a card (not fixed here):**
  - A name held only by stored rows in two packages, one of them disabled, with no registry holder. It answers by save order: the plain read gives 404 or the enabled row, and `/layers` gives 409 naming the disabled package. No disabled body is served.
  - The environment holds its own item of a name that an enabled and a disabled package also ship. `servedHolderAddressOf` steps aside, and the bare `/layers` code layer is still the first composite in registration order, which can be the disabled holder's.

## Verification

Every run used a worktree under `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (slot `dev-32183`), on a shared box. The base is `main` at de141e32, and `main` was merged in at e31ea52a and 9bff554e. Unless a line names another commit, everything ran on **1b655c3cd**, the pushed head, with a clean tree.

- **Build:** `turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs'` ran 119/119 tasks, exit 0.
- **Typecheck** (`pnpm typecheck`, with `check:test-typecheck`): run with a 6 GB heap for every package, because the cli test layer runs out of memory at the default. Packages: metadata-protocol, metadata, objectql, rest, runtime, core, cli, plugin-security, plugin-email, plugin-sharing, service-automation and plugin-approvals. All exit 0.
- **Lint:** root eslint (`--no-inline-config`) over the `src` of those twelve packages: exit 0.
- **Changeset gates:**
  - `check-adr-0087-registration`: `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
  - `check-changeset-no-major`: no `major` bump.
- **Dispatch gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` printed 84 commands.
  - Each one ran with its exit code recorded before any pipe, and all 84 exit 0.
  - `--ran`: "84 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 84 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- **Pre-push:** `check:commit-card-trailers` passed on both new commits. In the previous round it refused card references in five unpublished commit messages, and those were reworded before that push (tree unchanged).
- **Dogfood battery:** still owed: once, on the final head, after the qualifier hunk (narrowing arm).
